### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/service-automation`, touching **1** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/automation/connectors/credential-refs (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/automation/connectors/credential-refs (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 57cde8cb3da5970f2c3f6512569cacdb9b2b06a8` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `24da27e0016effe8cff59cb78a3df940d57dcde5` — the merge of head `ac6202e4f5ddc09d7460df964952ef4f5c4f6b51` into base `57cde8cb3da5970f2c3f6512569cacdb9b2b06a8`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 24da27e0016effe8cff59cb78a3df940d57dcde5 && git checkout 24da27e0016effe8cff59cb78a3df940d57dcde5
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 57cde8cb3da5970f2c3f6512569cacdb9b2b06a8 ac6202e4f5ddc09d7460df964952ef4f5c4f6b51 && git checkout -B drift-repro 57cde8cb3da5970f2c3f6512569cacdb9b2b06a8 && git merge --no-ff ac6202e4f5ddc09d7460df964952ef4f5c4f6b51

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 57cde8cb3da5970f2c3f6512569cacdb9b2b06a8
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 57cde8cb3da5970f2c3f6512569cacdb9b2b06a8` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The narrowing is exactly the 28 keys, and none has a reader.** The `en.ts` hunks remove 25 `packagedAutomation.*` leaves (12 flows-list, 13 clone-dialog), `home.quickActions.manageObjects`, `home.quickActions.manageObjectsDesc` and `layout.systemNav.objectManager`; the other nine packs remove the same leaves (−28 each; `zh` −32/+4 is the same 28 plus a rewritten group comment). My own grep on `main` for every removed full key finds no `t()` or typed reader anywhere: the only occurrences are the two pin tests this PR amends, two history comments in `de-quote-pairing-3876`, CHANGELOG text and the pending changeset `27378-…` (a historical "new key" sentence). The bare-leaf collisions (`title`, `subtitle`, `colActions`, `emptyTitle`, `loadFailed`, `clone`) are other namespaces (`ApprovalsInboxPage`'s `tr()` helper and non-i18n code), not these keys. Right.
- **Every key still read survives.** The leaves `main` reads under `packagedAutomation.` are the 20 of the Packaged actions page (`actionsHeading`, `actionsSubtitle`, `actionsEmptyTitle/Body`, `actionsLoadFailed`, `actionToggleLabel`, `actionOff*`, `colAction`, `colObject`, `colActivation`, `switchedOn/Off`, `toggleFailed(Http)`, `refresh`, `on`, `off`, `cancel`); all 20 are present in `en.ts` at the head. The surviving set equals the read set, with nothing read removed and nothing dead kept under the prefixes. Right.
- **Public surface:** `@object-ui/i18n`'s exported `TranslationKeys` loses 28 nested keys. A string-typed `t('…')` keeps compiling and echoes the key; a typed index (`TranslationKeys['packagedAutomation']['cloneCreated']`) fails with TS2339, which the dev measured on a rebuilt `dist`. That is the declared `(narrowing)`; the runtime contract (fallback to key) is unchanged. Right.
- `namespaces/studio` carries none of these keys, so no second pack moves. Right. No security-relevant finding; nothing withheld from this record.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset: `@object-ui/i18n` patch, `refactor(i18n)!:`, **BREAKING** banner, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` at line start in the changeset and the PR body. Under the repo's level rule (a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` with its BREAKING banner), `patch` is the required grade. Right.
- The migration the rule demands for a removed export is present: the FROM → TO table lists all 28 keys, each with "none" and the one-line fix (delete the reference), and the surviving set is named. Right.
- ADR-0087 disposition: `not-required (runtime-interface-only ui/packages/i18n/src/locales/en.ts#TranslationKeys)` with the reason (no Zod schema, no spec declaration, no stored metadata reads the key type; the compiler is the channel). Correct class: no authorable spec key or stored document names these keys, so no D2 conversion or D3 entry is owed. Right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Tier S**, no governed path; the seat's ACCEPT lands it after a green head and this record. The 维护者速读 says the maintainer owes nothing, which is right for Tier S.
- **Option A (retire the 7 NEEDS-REVIEW keys with the 21 CONFIRMED ones)** — the seat's amendment 6575664582. Verified above: each of the seven's footprint is history text or a pin, never a reader. Taking them now avoids a second narrowing later. Accepted.
- **Pending changeset `27378-packaged-automation-not-running-switch.md`** still says "new key `packagedAutomation.notRunningDeploymentPolicy`". It describes that PR's own change truthfully and ships in the same release as this removal; editing a pending changeset one did not add would trip `check-empty-changeset`, and this one is not false. Observation only; no action.
- Dev deviations: the `main` merge brought other key additions and touched none of the 28 (dead-key count under the prefixes still 0 at the head); the reverse TS2339 probe was deleted and the tree left clean. No open questions.

### ④ Design judgment

**`ui/packages/i18n/src/locales/en.ts` (and the nine sibling packs)** — judged against the readers on `main` and the dead-keys gate.
- The cut is along the retired screens' boundary, not along a prefix: `packagedAutomation` keeps the actions half intact and the shared keys (`refresh`, `cancel`, `on`, `off`, `toggleFailed(Http)`) that the actions page reads, so the group's reader set is unchanged. Break attempt: remove the whole group — the Packaged actions page would lose 20 live keys; the diff does not do that. Holds.
- The group comment is rewritten to describe what remains (actions page; flows half retired into Studio's Automations pillar, ADR-0146 D11) and drops the "both sections" and clone sentences that would now be false; the ADR-0126 §9 no-drift-wording rule and the `*Failed*` fallback note are kept. `zh` carries the same rewrite; the other eight packs' translator notes are untouched, which is right (they are terminology notes, not structure). Holds.
- Pack parity: the `all-locales-key-parity` and `en-zh-key-parity` pins hold the ten packs to one key set, so a pack that missed a removal would red; −28 in each of nine packs matches `en`. Holds.

**The two amended pins** — judged against what they pin.
- `dead-key-batch-retired-4730`: the two rows leave SURVIVING because the keys no longer exist; the pin's remaining rows are unchanged, so it still proves the #4730 batch's survivors. `de-quote-pairing-3876`: 104 → 103 with a history line in both assertions, because `cloneCreated`'s German value held one `„{{name}}“` pair; the durable identity `close === open + rdq` is untouched. Both are pins on the removed keys, not on behaviour. Holds.

**`connector-credentials-ui.ts`** — comment only; the new wording names the entry and component ref that exist on `main` (`automation:packaged-actions`). Holds.

No must-fix found. No should-fix.
